title: Form usability, privacy, and safe handling of user input
learningObjectives: Use form usability, privacy, and safe handling of user input accessibly and safely.

understand.concept: Collect only necessary data, use HTTPS, protect sensitive values and never trust client validation alone.
understand.whyItMatters: Correct form structure improves usability, accessibility and data safety.
understand.analogy: Think of a well-labelled application form.
understand.analogyLimit: Browser checks alone do not make submitted data trustworthy; the server must validate it.

explain.narrative: Collect only necessary data, use HTTPS, protect sensitive values and never trust client validation alone.

examples.code: <form><label for="name">Display name</label><input id="name" name="displayName" autocomplete="name"><button type="submit">Save</button></form>
examples.explanation: Inspect labels, types and validation for each control.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser renders the form controls and provides native behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Modify the example and operate every control using the keyboard.
practise.independentTask: Build an accessible registration form that respects privacy.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Form usability, privacy, and safe handling of user input</title></head><body>
<form><label for="name">Display name</label><input id="name" name="displayName" autocomplete="name"><button type="submit">Save</button></form>
</body></html>
practice.resetCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Form usability, privacy, and safe handling of user input</title></head><body>

</body></html>
